senses.gloss:
cīnācāra
(‘practice obtaining in Cīnā’)
------------------------------------------
See VĀMĀCĀRA.

cinmudrā
(‘hand-pose indicating knowledge’)
------------------------------------------
Icons of deities, sages and saints, sculptured as per the rules given in the standard works of इचोनोग्रफ्य्, usually have certain hand-poses called ‘hasta’ or ‘mudrā’, indicating certain specific ideas or sentiments. One such pose, the ‘cinmudrā,’ is sculptured on images in the posture of imparting knowledge. For instance: दक्षिणामूर्ति aspect of शिव and Ādiśaṅkara. In this pose the tips of the thumb and the forefinger, usually of the right hand, are joined to form a circle while the other fingers are kept open and stretched. The whole palm faces outwards.
This मुद्रा is also called ‘vyākhyāna or sandeśa’ मुद्रा.
See MUDRĀS.

Cintāmaṇi
(‘thought-gem’)
------------------------------------------
The पुराणस् describe this supernatural gem, the possessor of which is said to obtain whatever he wishes for (maṇi = gem; cintā = thought, wish).
In devotional literature, God is des-cribed as चिन्तामणि for the same reason.
In अस्त्रोलोग्य्, a particular combination of प्लनेत्स् heralding an auspicious time for travelling is called चिन्तामणि.
In Buddhist symbology, it stands for the मिन्द्.
